title: DNA and Mutations
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: DNA and Mutations Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: DNA is a double helix of nucleotides with complementary base pairs; DNA replicates before cell division; genes code for proteins; mutations change the DNA and may change traits. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 3: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Life Science): DNA structure, replication, genes and proteins, kinds of mutations and their effects. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A pairs with T; C pairs with G.
key_sub: A mutation is a change in the DNA.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is made of two strands twisted into a double helix. Each nucleotide has a sugar, a phosphate and a base; the bases pair A–T and C–G. Before a cell divides, DNA copies itself: each strand is a template for a new one.

Genes are sections of DNA that code for proteins, which produce traits. A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence; it may be harmful, helpful or have no effect. Radiation and some chemicals increase the rate of mutations.

Example

Strand ATGC. Complementary strand?

A–T, C–G

Answer: TACG

Example

Is every mutation harmful?

Think of variation.

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Pairing A with G.
  • Thinking mutations always cause disease.
  • Thinking genes and chromosomes are the same.

faq.q: Why must DNA be copied before cell division?
faq.a: So that each new cell gets a full set of DNA.

faq.q: How can mutations help a species?
faq.a: They create variation; some new traits help organisms survive.

items.q: A DNA segment has 3,380 base pairs. How many hydrogen bonds hold it together if 30% of its bases are adenine?
items.e: A = T = 30%, G = C = 20%. A–T pairs = 2028 (2 bonds), G–C pairs = 1,352 (3 bonds): total = 8,112.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 32% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are cytosine (C)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 32%. A + T = 64%, so G + C = 36% and G = C = 18%.

items.e: Effects depend on how the protein changes and on the environment.
